paper.title: Which LLM to Play? Convergence-Aware Online Model Selection with Time-Increasing Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Time-increasing bandits with increasing-then-converging trend (linear increase then abrupt change to stable value c_i)
unmapped: Rested rising bandit: expected reward of arm i depends on its own number of pulls n_i(t), mu_i(t)=mu_{i,n_i(t)}
Reward increases linearly in the pull count until an unknown converging point nu_i, then abruptly becomes a stable value c_i
Regret is measured against the optimal (greedy) pull sequence n_i^*(T)
settings.definition_quote: we assume the reward received by each arm $i$ first increases linearly with the number of times it is pulled, and then abruptly changes to a stable value $c_i$ within the range of $[0, T]$, where $T$ remains unknown.

symbols.C_over: sum of stable values c_i over arms i with n_i(T) >= n_i^*(T) (pulled at least as often as in the optimal sequence)
symbols.L: a constant smaller than ln T
symbols.Delta_min: min over t in [0,T] and i != i_t^* of mu_{i_t^*}(t) - mu_i(t)

conditions: reward of each arm increases linearly in its pull count then abruptly changes to stable value c_i
optimal arm unique in each round (assumed in proof of Lemma 2)
tuning: window omega large enough (proof of Lemma 5)

source.label: sec:regret:thm
source.quote: Assume that $\delta \leq {1}/{T}$, then the expected regret of TI-UCB algorithm is bounded by \EE{R(T)} \leq \sum_{i:n_i(T)\geq n_{i}^{\ast}(T)} c_i \frac{4096 \ln(T)}{\Delta_{\min}^2}  + K\left(\frac{2\pi^2}{3} + \omega + 2 + 2L \right) + 2, where $\Delta_{\min}$ ... is the minimum gap between the optimal reward and the true reward and $L$ is a constant smaller than $\ln T$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards against the optimal greedy pull sequence; recorded as pseudo_regret vs best_policy. The proof is loose (final derivation gives K(pi^2/3+1)+K*omega+2KL+2, differing from the theorem statement); theorem statement recorded. Sum is over arms with n_i(T)>=n_i^*(T), a random set, encoded via declared symbol C_over. Environment mapped to markovian + rotting_or_rising because rewards depend on pull counts (rested rising bandit). Paper summarizes as O(log T / Delta_min^2).
